subject: Decisioning playbook: evaluation sprint and region lock
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Wallace <sarah.wallace@medicore.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Decisioning playbook: evaluation sprint and region lock

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, I’m sending a lightweight MAP (attached) and a proposed evaluation sprint that surfaces the deployment-mode decision early so Medicore can lock region/residency needs before deep integration. High-level suggested milestones: 

- Week 0 (by 2026-07-24): MAP kickoff + security questionnaire returned (I attached v2 of the MAP).
- Week 1 (by 2026-07-28): Deployment-mode decision point (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — we want to lock this before data ingestion testing.
- Week 2 (by 2026-08-04): Region residency verification and baseline latency tests in candidate regions (eu-west-1 preferred).
- Week 3–4: Feature evals, cost modeling, and closing window.

Decision drivers for the deployment-mode milestone we’ll use in the MAP: data residency, throughput SLAs, audit/KMS requirements, and procurement lead times. If Medicore requires EU-only data-at-rest and an on-prem presence, Private is the path; otherwise Dedicated (reserved GPUs in eu region) or Hosted with EU tenancy and KMS options are likely.

Please review the attached MAP and the security questionnaire you mentioned; if you can return that spreadsheet by end of week we’ll use it to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated constraints.

Proposed next steps:
- Sarah: share the completed security spreadsheet (attaching a template).
- MedCore: confirm whether EU data-at-rest is a hard requirement and any timeline constraints for August launch windows.
- Redwood: we’ll prepare a dedicated-trial pricing stub and a short region-comparison note for your SRE.

I’m happy to hop on a 30-min working session — I’ve tentatively left a 60-min kickoff link in the MAP (or pick a slot here: https://calendly.com/redwood/kickoff-60).

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: 20260721-MAP-v2.pdf
From: Sarah Wallace <sarah.wallace@medicore.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medicore.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decisioning playbook: evaluation sprint and region lock

Thanks, Irene — this looks good and aligns with our internal timeline. A few immediate clarifications from our side: 

- EU data-at-rest: this is a hard requirement for patient-identifiable metadata. We need confirmation that any storage or persistent keys will be in eu-west-1 (or equivalent) by August 4.
- Audit/KMS: we require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for production and a SOC2 attestation for the hosting option.
- Procurement: we have a 30–45 day procurement cycle for any committed contracts; if we choose Dedicated, we’ll need committed capacity detail for budgeting.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire (medi_core_security_q3_2026.xlsx). Can your security team fill the SOC2 evidence section and confirm the KMS story (hosted vs dedicated vs private differences)?

Also, we’d like a short note that outlines the expected differences in cost and average token latency between Hosted (EU tenancy), a Dedicated reserved pool in eu-west-1, and a Private on-prem deploy so our CTO can weigh trade-offs.

Best,
Sarah Wallace
Head of AI Product | MediCore Health
Attachment: medi_core_security_q3_2026.xlsx
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Wallace <sarah.wallace@medicore.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decisioning playbook: evaluation sprint and region lock

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick follow. I went through the questionnaire and pulled a short technical summary below that we can expand into the MAP appendix: 

1) Data residency and KMS
- Hosted: We can guarantee EU data-at-rest by pinning tenancy to eu-west-1 and integrating with customer KMS via our KMS connectors (BYOK supported for production tiers). For the Hosted path we’ll provide a dedicated tenant in eu-west-1 with encryption keys under customer control.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools run in the customer’s preferred region; provisioned in eu-west-1 for your case. BYOK and HSM workflows available; offers lower cross-region egress and predictable latency.
- Private (on-prem): Full on-prem bundle; you manage the storage and keys, we provide the runtime and orchestrator.

2) SOC2 and evidence
- We have SOC2 Type II artifacts for our hosted control plane; for Dedicated we can provide scoped SOC2 evidence and a deployment checklist to map customer audit needs to host-level controls. I’ll mark items in your spreadsheet where we can attach evidence and where we need tenant-specific confirmations.

3) Performance and cost delta (short note)
- Hosted (eu tenancy): fastest path to start; slightly higher per-token variability but lowest time-to-value. Expected median generation latency ~ 65–90 ms per 256-token chunk (depends on model).
- Dedicated (eu-west-1 reserved): better tail latency and throughput consistency; ~ 50–70 ms median for same profile; unit cost improves under reserved commitments.
- Private: best isolation, predictable at scale, but longest lead time and ops overhead.

I’ll attach a short pricing stub for a 3-month Dedicated trial and mark the procurement timeline items. We can also run a quick latency smoke test in eu-west-1 next week if you confirm hostnames and sample payloads.

On the MAP timeline: we can move the Deployment-mode decision to 2026-07-28 as proposed, but to hit your Aug 4 residency date we’d need the security spreadsheet back by EOD Friday (7/24).

—Dev
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: dedicated-trial-pricing-stub.pdf

All — thanks for the clarity and the quick turn. We’ll proceed with a focused evaluation on Dedicated in eu-west-1 with Hosted (eu tenancy) as a fallback for initial experiments. Action items on our side:

- I will return the completed security spreadsheet by EOD Friday (7/24).
- Tom (CTO) will schedule a 60-min kickoff with your team for Monday 7/27; he prefers a 10:00 CET slot — I’ll confirm via the Calendly link.
- Procurement will review the Dedicated trial stub; expect questions around committed capacity and termination notice.

Please treat the Deployment-mode decision as locked to Dedicated for the MAP milestone (we’ll use Hosted only for early-stage exploration). Looking forward to the latency smoke test — we’ll send sample payloads this afternoon.

Regards,
Sarah Wallace
Head of AI Product | MediCore Health
